papers.title: Ginsenoside Rb1 alleviates uterine aging via AMPK-mediated mTOR inactivation.
papers.authors: Ping Zhou; Yue Wang; Ming Cheng; Feng Deng; Fenting Liu; Xiunan Chen; Ke Ning; Dan Mo; Zhonghong Zeng; Ziying Huang; Yunshu Dong; Yinxue Wang; Chao Zhang; Jie Qiao; Yang Yu; Heng Pan; Rong Li
papers.abstract: Uterine aging impairs fertility and reproductive health, but the underlying pathogenic mechanisms and effective treatment strategies remain elusive. Defective endometrial decidualization and implantation failure are hallmarks of uterine aging, which can be driven by cellular senescence, especially in endometrial stromal cells (EnSCs). Rb1 has been reported to relieve cellular senescence by suppressing oxidative and inflammatory pathways. However, whether Rb1 functions in alleviating uterine aging remains uncertain. Here, we demonstrate that Rb1 can attenuate oxidative stress, senescence, and apoptosis in the EnSCs of the aging human endometrium and murine uterus. Further proteomic analysis reveals that Rb1 safeguards against endometrial aging by regulating mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR)-related pathways. Rb1 treatment results in the activation of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and AMPK-mediated suppression of the mTOR-nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) signaling loop, thereby ameliorating aging-related phenotypes. Collectively, our findings illustrate that Rb1 alleviates uterine aging by attenuating endometrial stromal cell senescence and suppressing AMPK-mTOR-NF-κB-driven inflammatory signaling. Rather than selectively eliminating senescent cells, Rb1 primarily targets senescence-associated dysfunction and restores endometrial homeostasis, highlighting its potential as a senescence-modulating therapeutic strategy for uterine aging.

papers.title: pH‐Responsive Nanoplatform‐Mediated Lipid Hijacking and Metabolic Collapse for Synergistic Starvation‐Immunotherapy
papers.authors: Xianlong Zong; Haochen Yao; Danyang Shen; Furu Gong; Zixuan Wang; Haoyang Qin; Yang Yang; Ruirui Qiao; Yongjuan Li; Rui Li
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Tumor starvation therapy is a promising metabolism‐targeting intervention, yet its efficacy is largely counteracted by lipid droplet (LD)‐driven compensatory metabolism in malignant cells. Existing LDs‐targeted approaches are further hampered by off‐target systemic metabolic disturbances and inherent immunosuppressive adverse effects. Here, we construct a zeolitic imidazolate framework‐8 (ZIF‐8)‐based nanomedicine loaded with 2‐deoxy‐D‐glucose (2‐DG) and surface‐decorated with copper‐tannic acid (Cu‐TA, ZIF‐8/2‐DG@Cu‐TA). This nanosystem reroutes intracellular LDs from tumor cells to adjacent cancer‐associated fibroblasts (CAFs) to realize synergistic tumor starvation and immunotherapy. In the acidic tumor microenvironment, the degradable Cu‐TA coating activates connexin 43 (Cx43) hemichannels on CAFs. After internalization by tumor cells, ZIF‐8/2‐DG releases 2‐DG to suppress glycolysis, while dissociated zinc ions disrupt mitochondrial bioenergetics and further trigger Cx43 hemichannels activation on tumor cells. Fully assembled Cx43 gap junctions mediate directional LDs trafficking from tumor cells to CAFs, restricting intracellular lipid energy pools sustaining malignant metabolic demands. Simultaneous blockade of glycolysis, mitochondrial respiration and lipid metabolism induces profound tumor‐cell metabolic collapse. The resulting metabolic stress strongly amplifies antitumor immunity and markedly suppresses both subcutaneous and orthotopic MOC1 tumors. Overall, this study establishes a gap‐junction‐driven triple metabolic starvation paradigm and offers mechanistic insights for next‐generation metabolic immunotherapies.

papers.title: A Bi‐Adjuvant Senolytic Nanovaccine Modulating Dendritic Cell Senescence Ameliorates Aging‐Related Metabolic Dysfunction
papers.authors: Qingxu Song; Xiaoxue Du; Wenbo Dong; Ying Wang; Xiaojing Wang; Qiliang Yin
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Senolytic vaccines hold promise for eliminating senescent cells, but their efficacy is limited by poor seno‐antigen immunogenicity and age‐related dendritic cell (DC) dysfunction. Here, we engineered an active biomaterial‐enabled bi‐adjuvant senolytic nanovaccine (CK5‐GC‐NV) by co‐assembling CpG oligodeoxynucleotide with a fusion protein of the seno‐antigen Gpnmb and a cationic spider silk protein variant (CK5). Beyond antigen delivery, the CK5 scaffold acts as an intrinsic senomodulator associated with the downregulation of mitotic kinases Aurka/b and a concomitant decrease in senescence‐associated PI3K/AKT phosphorylation in DCs. This intervention attenuates aged DC phenotypes, restores antigen cross‐presentation, and synergizes with CpG to elicit potent cytotoxic T‐lymphocyte responses against senescent targets. Across multiple aging mouse models, CK5‐GC‐NV immunization orchestrated targeted clearance of Gpnmb + senescent adipocytes, profoundly ameliorating metabolic dysfunction and extending lifespan. This multifunctional biomaterial platform integrates seno‐antigen immunogenicity enhancement with the restoration of aged DC function, providing a promising proof‐of‐concept for antigen‐directed gerotherapeutics.

papers.title: DUSP26 Regulated by YY1 Lactylation Couples Osteogenesis and Angiogenesis by Dephosphorylating PMPCB at Y141 and Activating Mitophagy in BMSCs
papers.authors: Yunpeng Lv; Feng Wu; Xiongjie Liang; Chong Liu; Wenhui Guo; Kejian Zhang; Jiawen Niu; Wenjie Jiang; Hongjian Xu; Anlong Jiang; Yang Zheng; Enming Yu; Xintao Wang; Jinglong Yan; Jingjun Xia; Chengchao Song
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) support bone formation through osteogenic differentiation and pro‐angiogenic paracrine activity, but the mechanisms coordinating these functions remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified dual‐specificity phosphatase 26 (DUSP26) as a regulator of BMSC osteogenesis and mitochondrial homeostasis. DUSP26 expression increased during osteogenic differentiation and was reduced in osteoporotic femoral tissues. p300 gain‐ and loss‐of‐function experiments, together with analysis of the Yin Yang1(YY1) K183R mutant, supported the conclusion that p300‐regulated YY1 lactylation contributes to DUSP26 transcriptional activation. DUSP26 interacted with the mitochondrial processing peptidase subunit beta(PMPCB) and reduced its tyrosine phosphorylation, with mass spectrometry and mutational analyses implicating Y141 as involved in this regulation. Functional assays supported a model in which DUSP26 limits mitochondrial processing peptidase (MPP)‐mediated PTEN‐induced kinase 1 (PINK1) processing and promotes PINK1‐dependent mitophagy, thereby supporting mitochondrial homeostasis. DUSP26 enhanced osteogenic differentiation and the pro‐angiogenic activity of BMSC‐conditioned medium(CM), whereas its knockdown impaired bone formation and reduced type H vessels in vivo. Furthermore, BMSC‐derived exosomes carrying a runt‐related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2) promoter‐driven DUSP26 plasmid produced preferential transgene expression in osteogenic‐lineage cells and attenuated ovariectomy‐induced bone loss in mice. These findings link lactylation‐associated transcriptional regulation to mitochondrial protein processing and support further preclinical evaluation of DUSP26‐directed approaches for osteoporosis.

papers.title: Intermittent Fasting Alleviates Diabetes-Associated Cognitive Impairment Through FGF21-Mediated Lipid Remodeling and Mitochondrial Redox Regulation
papers.authors: Fen Xiong; Kaiyuan Jiang; Xiaoqing Yan; Tian Tang; Xinran Wang; Yiwen Peng; Ruoxin Guan; Xi Zhang; Chen Li; Hongchang Gao
papers.abstract: Background: Cognitive impairment is a clinically relevant neurological complication of diabetes, yet its metabolic mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to determine whether fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21), a fasting-responsive metabolic hormone, mediates the neuroprotective effects of intermittent fasting (IF) in diabetes-associated cognitive impairment, and to explore the underlying mechanisms. Methods: Streptozotocin (STZ)-induced type 1 diabetes-associated cognitive impairment (T1DCI) mice were used together with FGF21 genetic deletion and exogenous FGF21 supplementation. Cognitive function, neuronal injury, hippocampal lipid metabolism, mitochondrial function, protein acetylation, and SIRT3-associated deacetylation were evaluated. Results: IF significantly increased FGF21 levels in serum and hippocampus and improved cognitive deficits, whereas these effects were attenuated in FGF21-deficient mice. FGF21 supplementation improved cognitive performance and attenuated neuronal damage, accompanied by MAPK-related signaling changes. Lipidomic analysis revealed decreased phosphatidylcholine and triacylglycerols in the hippocampus of T1DCI mice, which were partially restored by FGF21. Consistently, FGF21 increased the expression of LPIN3, DGAT2, and CHPT1, key enzymes involved in PC and TAG biosynthesis. FGF21 also improved mitochondrial function and was associated with reduced protein acetylation, while SIRT3 inhibition attenuated these effects. Conclusions: These findings suggest that FGF21 contributes to the neuroprotective effects of IF in diabetes-associated cognitive impairment, potentially through coordinated regulation of lipid metabolism and mitochondrial function.

papers.title: Distinct Epigenetic Responses to Aging and Short‐Term High‐Fat Diet in Hepatic Lipid Metabolism Genes in Male and Female Mice
papers.authors: Annalena Frank; Sascha Tierling; Beate Czepukojc; Sonja M. Kessler; Thomas Hentrich; Michael Kohlstedt; Johannes Haybaeck; Christoph Wittmann; Jessica Hoppstädter; Julia Schulze‐Hentrich; Alexandra K. Kiemer
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Aging is associated with widespread epigenetic remodelling that contributes to metabolic alterations in the liver. High‐fat diet (HFD) represents a major environmental perturbation affecting hepatic metabolism, yet its specific impact on age‐associated epigenetic changes remains unclear. Here, we investigated in male and female mice whether HFD induces epigenetic changes similar to or distinct from those observed during aging, with a particular focus on DNA methylation (5mC) and hydroxymethylation (5hmC) in key lipid metabolism genes. Methods We combined re‐analysis of published RNA‐sequencing datasets from young and aged mouse livers with targeted epigenetic and metabolic profiling in a short‐term HFD model. Results In our study, we identified a consistent age‐associated transcriptional upregulation of lipogenic genes, including fatty acid synthase ( Fasn ) and stearoyl‐CoA 9‐desaturase ( Scd1 ), accompanied by reduced DNA methylation and gene‐specific alterations in 5hmC. In contrast, HFD exposure resulted in increased gene‐body methylation with reduced expression of these genes, alongside shifts in fatty acid composition indicative of altered lipid metabolism. Analyses of samples from male and female mice showed sex‐specific differences. Notably, the applied HFD model did not induce overt lipid pathology, suggesting that these changes reflect early metabolic adaptation rather than advanced disease states. Conclusions Together, our findings indicate that HFD induces an epigenetic and transcriptional response in hepatic lipid metabolism genes that differs from and in part opposes age‐associated patterns. These results support a model in which short‐term dietary lipid excess triggers distinct regulatory mechanisms rather than simply recapitulating epigenetic aging.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis reveals ApoLp ‐ III ‐mediated BmNPV suppression via host energy and lipid reprogramming
papers.authors: Quadsia Jabeen; Xinhao Jiao; Zi Liang; Na Zhang; Shengyan Xiao; Wenwen Jiang; Shuyi Liu; Aniqa Shakoor Butt; Ping Wu
papers.abstract: Abstract In global sericulture, the most economically important and primary causative pathogen is Bombyx mori nucleopolyhedrovirus (BmNPV), but the host immune metabolism that restricts the viral replication is not completely defined. A recently identified insect multifunctional apolipoprotein (apolipophorin‐III [ApoLp‐III]) was shown to suppress BmNPV proliferation by enhancing ceramide accumulation. However, it is unknown how this antiviral action is mediated through coordinated transcriptional and metabolic changes. In this study, we dissect the ApoLp‐III‐mediated antiviral mechanism by constructing an ApoLp‐III‐overexpressing BmN cell line and integrating RNA‐seq data with a previously published metabolomic profile. A total of 1067 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) with significantly opposing expression trends were identified. These DEGs were prominent in DNA replication, oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) and amino sugar nucleotide sugar metabolism. Genes associated with amino acid metabolism were down‐regulated, while genes linked with DNA replication and OXPHOS were up‐regulated. Bidirectional regulation of sphingolipids was also confirmed by quantitative real‐time PCR (qRT‐PCR) and transcriptomic data. Ceramide accumulation resulted from the down‐regulation of alkaline ceramidase ( ACER ) and up‐regulation of regulatory subunit of the rate‐limiting ceramide synthesis enzyme, SPTssA . Integrated multi‐omics correlation analysis further showed that ceramide species positively correlated with OXPHOS and negatively correlated with amino sugar metabolism. Meanwhile, down‐regulated triglycerides showed negative correlation with DNA replication and OXPHOS genes. In addition, we identified ApoLp‐III interacting proteins, that is, the integrin‐associated cytoskeletal regulator, Talin‐1 and lepidopteran‐specific immune receptor Haemolin, using Flag‐based co‐immunoprecipitation coupled with mass spectrometry. Our results show that ApoLp‐III suppresses BmNPV replication by the coordinated reprogramming of host cellular energy (OXPHOS) and lipid (sphingolipid) metabolism. Thus, ApoLp‐III acts as an important immunometabolic hub in the antiviral defence of lepidopterans, and our research also offers a theoretical foundation for controlling silkworm diseases by targeting sphingolipid‐energy pathway.

papers.title: Bacteroidota‐derived glycine lipids differentially regulate skeletal muscle mitochondrial adaptation during Western diet feeding in male Ldlr −/− mice
papers.authors: Siyun Kim; Sung Gi Noh; Minje Ji; Tomas Vence; Lidan Gao; Oliver Otoko; Frank C. Nichols; Christopher N. Blesso; Oh Sung Kwon
papers.abstract: Abstract The Western diet (WD) is associated with skeletal muscle mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired oxidative metabolism, redox imbalance and inflammation. Emerging evidence suggests that gut microbiome‐derived metabolites contribute to host metabolic regulation, yet the role of Bacteroidota‐derived glycine lipids in skeletal muscle remains unknown. This study tested whether two structurally related bacterial glycine lipids, lipid 654 (L654) and lipid 1256 (L1256), regulate skeletal muscle mitochondrial remodelling in WD‐fed Ldlr −/− mice. Male Ldlr −/− mice were fed a normal chow or WD and administered L654, L1256 or vehicle control for 8 weeks. Skeletal muscle glycine lipid accumulation, mitochondrial respiration, mitochondrial biogenesis markers, mitophagy‐associated signalling, inflammatory and antioxidant proteins and muscle fibre cross‐sectional area were assessed. L1256, but not L654, accumulated in skeletal muscle. Functionally, L1256 selectively enhanced fatty acid‐supported mitochondrial respiration and increased respiratory control ratio. L1256 also increased peroxisome proliferator‐activated receptor gamma coactivator 1‐alpha (PGC‐1α), mitochondrial transcription factor A (TFAM) and electron transport chain complexes IV and V, suggesting enhanced oxidative mitochondrial remodelling. In parallel, L1256 altered markers associated with mitochondrial quality control signalling, increased nuclear factor erythroid 2‐related factor 2 (Nrf2), manganese superoxide dismutase (MnSOD) and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), suppressed nuclear factor kappa‐light‐chain‐enhancer of activated B cells (NF‐κB) signalling and preserved muscle fibre cross‐sectional area. L654 upregulated mitochondrial biogenesis transcripts without altering protein abundance. These findings identify L1256 as a microbiome‐derived lipid retained within skeletal muscle that enhanced oxidative metabolism and preserved mitochondrial quality signalling under metabolic stress. The data suggest that tissue retention of bacterial lipids may be an important determinant of skeletal muscle mitochondrial adaptation. image Key points Western diet contributes to skeletal muscle mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired oxidative metabolism and chronic inflammation. Microbiome‐derived glycine lipids are bioactive molecules from Bacteroidota species, but their effects on skeletal muscle mitochondrial metabolism remain poorly understood. Bacteroidota‐derived glycine lipids produce distinct skeletal muscle responses in Western diet‐fed Ldlr − / − mice, where lipid 1256 accumulated in skeletal muscle and enhanced fatty acid‐supported respiration, whereas lipid 654 primarily induced transcriptional responses without detectable tissue accumulation. Lipid 1256 increased peroxisome proliferator‐activated receptor gamma coactivator 1‐alpha (PGC‐1α), mitochondrial transcription factor A (TFAM) and complexes IV and V of the electron transport chain together with restoration of Parkin, nuclear factor erythroid 2‐related factor 2 (Nrf2), manganese superoxide dismutase (MnSOD) and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) while reducing nuclear factor kappa‐light‐chain‐enhancer of activated B cells (NF‐κB) and interleukin 6 (IL‐6) expression and preserving skeletal muscle cross‐sectional area. These findings suggest that gut microbiome‐derived glycine lipids are regulators of skeletal muscle mitochondrial metabolism, and that tissue retention of bacterial lipids influences mitochondrial oxidative remodelling during metabolic stress.

papers.title: Mitochondrial dysfunction in Parkinson's disease and aging
papers.authors: Xiaoyu Lu; Zhiyan Huang; Zhongming Ying
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder for which advancing age is the major risk factor. Aging and PD share several features, including chronic neuroinflammation and pathological protein accumulation. This overlap suggests that mechanisms driving the aging process may also contribute to the onset and progression of PD. In this narrative review, we examine mitochondrial dysfunction as a shared feature of aging and PD, focusing on energy production, calcium buffering, apoptosis, inflammation, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. The literature reviewed here suggests shared alterations in mitochondrial dynamics, increased mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) instability, NAD + depletion, Complex I inhibition, redox imbalance, and disrupted calcium homeostasis. We also summarize mitochondria-targeted interventions investigated in PD.

papers.title: Cancer as a syntrophic cellular consortium established by fatty acid oxidation–primed mitochondria and carrier macrophages
papers.authors: Abhijit Deonath
papers.abstract: The escalating clinical link between cardiovascular disease and subsequent cancer suggests a systemic etiology beyond the sole purview of somatic mutation. This article reviews emerging evidence through a novel lens: cancer as a syntrophic cellular consortium, where metabolic stratification, driven by fatty acid oxidation (FAO)-primed mitochondria and mediated by carrier macrophages, establishes functionally distinct, metabolically interdependent cellular subpopulations. Stressed cardiomyocytes eject metabolically “primed” mitochondria. These organelles are engulfed by macrophages, transforming them into pathogenic “mito-macrophages” that act as mobile systemic carriers. These mito-macrophages instigate malignancy through mitochondrial transfer to recipient cells, inducing profound metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming. Within individual cells, the transferred mitochondria establish distinct intracellular oxidation zones fueled by FAO, juxtaposed with hypoxia zones favoring glycolysis. This primary compartmentalization scales up within the evolving tumor: cells from oxidation zones adopt a “leader” phenotype, characterized by high FAO, metabolic flexibility, and invasive capacity, while cells from hypoxia zones become “follower” phenotypes, relying on glycolysis and contributing to bulk tumor growth. Critical intercellular signaling pathways between these emerging “leader” and “follower” populations are central to establishing, maintaining, and propagating this obligate, syntrophic cross-feeding hierarchy, ensuring tumor progression. This framework bridges cardiac stress and distal cancer, elucidating how metabolic and epigenetic imprinting dictates cellular roles within a structured malignant consortium. Reconceiving cancer as such a syntrophic system offers new avenues for therapeutic intervention, targeting metabolic instigators and the signaling axes that define its consortium partners. This framework synthesizes established biological mechanisms into a novel, testable hypothesis and is presented as such. Direct experimental evidence for several of the proposed linkages—particularly long-distance macrophage-mediated trafficking of cardiomyocyte-derived mitochondria, and the FAO-primed state—remains to be established.

papers.title: Toward a comparative endocrinology of aging: insights from insects
papers.authors: Jiangtian Chen; Fernando G. Noriega; Marc Tatar
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Insulin-like signaling modulates aging and lifespan in insects. Here, we discuss a novel view of this control: insulin hormone in the adult regulates the production of the sesquiterpenoid juvenile hormone (JH) that in turn acts as the systemic regulator of aging and lifespan. Work in Drosophila establishes that insulin signaling is allatotropic – it stimulates the production and secretion of JH from the corpora allata. JH then exerts systemic effects on adult survival through its control of specific proteins, translation and proteostasis. The interdependent functions of insulin and JH allow reproduction and longevity to be coupled in many insects or decoupled in social insects with long-lived queens and in some long-lived genetic mutants of Drosophila. Features of these insulin-regulated life history syndromes are also found in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans. Recognizing the systemic role of JH in aging provides grounds to search for analogous systems in mammals that might modulate human lifespan.

papers.title: Gramine limits alcohol-associated liver injury by suppressing NOX1-linked ferroptotic responses and mitochondrial dysfunction.
papers.authors: Yu Zhang; Luxia Su; Heran Cheng; Wei Wei; Wenxuan Xu; Xiaofeng Bao; Chunfeng Lu
papers.abstract: Alcohol-associated liver injury involves oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and ferroptosis-related damage. NADPH oxidase 1 (NOX1), together with its regulatory GTPase Ras-related C3 botulinum toxin substrate 1 (RAC1), forms a regulatory module that governs redox signaling. Yet small molecules that engage NOX1 and suppress these coupled injury programs remain insufficiently defined. Here, we identified gramine as a candidate NOX1-engaging compound and delineated its protective mechanism in ethanol-associated hepatocellular injury. Alcohol challenge induced a hepatic NOX1/RAC1 response, recapitulated in ethanol-injured hepatocytes. Silencing Nox1 or Rac1 blunted ethanol-driven injury phenotypes, limiting injury-associated enzyme release, reactive oxygen species accumulation, mitochondrial membrane potential disturbance, mitochondrial network disruption, and DNA fragmentation while partially preserving glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4). Molecular docking predicted a gramine-NOX1 interaction, a cellular thermal shift assay supported target engagement, and cycloheximide chase analysis showed gramine accelerated NOX1 protein turnover. In ethanol-exposed hepatocytes, gramine conferred concentration-associated protection, improving cell viability, and reducing injury-associated enzyme release, lipid droplet signals, and DNA fragmentation. Post-ethanol gramine treatment reduced injury-associated enzyme release. NOX1 overexpression undermined gramine-mediated protection and reinstated ferrous iron accumulation, glutathione redox imbalance, reactive oxygen species production, mitochondrial dysfunction, and damage-associated signaling. Erastin weakened gramine-mediated protection, implicating inhibition of ferroptotic responses in the protective mechanism. In alcohol-gavaged mice, gramine reduced hepatic NOX1 abundance, serum injury markers, Fe2+ levels, lipid accumulation, and lipid peroxidation-associated changes, while preserving GPX4 abundance and limiting histopathological injury. These findings support gramine as a NOX1-engaging small molecule that limits alcohol-associated liver injury by suppressing NOX1-linked ferroptotic responses and mitochondrial dysfunction.

papers.title: Suppressing the SREBP-mediated lipogenic pathway rescues pink1 deficiency in Drosophila and influences mitochondrial morphology
papers.authors: Jenny Zhe Liao; Christopher Tam; Esther M. Verheyen
papers.abstract: Sterol-regulatory element binding proteins (SREBP) are master transcriptional factors controlling lipogenesis. In Drosophila, the SREBP-mediated lipogenic pathway is essential for development. Homozygous SREBP mutants are lipid deficient and larval lethal, whereas excessive lipids in flies are often associated with neurodegeneration. Since SREBP has previously been identified as a risk factor for Parkinson's disease, we further investigated the role of SREBP-mediated lipogenesis in a pink1 deficient Drosophila parkinsonism model. We found that expressing either dominant negative SREBP or knocking down its downstream target rescues pink1 mutant phenotypes including thorax indentation and impaired locomotion. Investigation of the indirect flight muscles reveals that suppression of the lipogenic pathway restores defective muscle morphology and mitochondrial defects, and reduces ectopic ROS associated with the pink1 null allele. Interestingly, we found altered mitochondrial morphologies when the lipogenic pathway was manipulated under physiological condition, suggesting the SREBP-mediated lipogenic pathway plays a role in regulating mitochondrial shapes. Our findings highlight the tight connection between lipid metabolism and mitochondria in both disease and physiological setting.

papers.title: The mitochondrion as a mechanometabolic conductor of cancer metastasis: pharmacological insights from the mitochondria–peroxisome interface
papers.authors: Subhajit Dutta; Namrata Maity
papers.abstract: Metastasis demands more than sustained ATP production: cancer cells must move organelles, remodel membranes, manage oxidative stress, and reprogram metabolism as they pass from invasion to distant colonisation. Mitochondria sit at the centre of this adaptation. This Review organises their contribution around four linked axes: deployment to the cell cortex and invadopodia; reactive oxygen species and metabolite signalling; VDAC1-dependent metabolite, calcium, apoptotic and mtDNA gating; and HIF-1α–BNIP3-dependent remodelling of the mitochondrial pool. We then ask how this mitochondrial programme is altered by peroxisomes. The two organelles share components of the fission machinery, coordinate lipid-derived substrate use and cellular redox balance, and divide tasks in hydrogen-peroxide control, ether-lipid synthesis, organelle quality control and MAVS signalling. These connections matter pharmacologically. A DRP1- or redox-directed intervention may affect both organelles, whereas VDAC1 provides a more mitochondria-restricted target logic. Peroxisomal pathways are also context dependent: fatty-acid shortening and ether-lipid synthesis can increase metabolic flexibility and membrane remodelling, yet the same pathways may raise oxidative stress or create ferroptotic susceptibility. By separating established molecular links from mechanisms that remain untested in metastatic models, we propose a hierarchical view in which mitochondria remain the principal mechanometabolic conductor, while peroxisomes set important boundary conditions for substrate use, redox signalling, immune responses and therapeutic selectivity. We also state the limitation this framing carries. The mitochondrial arm of the framework rests on direct experimental evidence, whereas a causal contribution of mitochondria–peroxisome contacts to invasion, transit or colonisation has not been demonstrated: it is inferred here from contact biology characterised without testing metastatic endpoints, from division machinery shared between the two organelles, and from biochemical coupling. The interface is therefore advanced as a testable framework for target selection and pharmacological attribution, not as an established driver of metastasis.

papers.title: Bisphenol A induces ACSL4-associated ferro-aging-like urothelial injury: Implications for Hunner-type interstitial cystitis.
papers.authors: Wenbo Wu; Yang Xu; Zhongwen Lu; Yang Zhang; Liyu Cai; Feng Gao; Zhuohan Niu; Dayuan Zong; Hui Wang; Peng Xue
papers.abstract: Hunner-type interstitial cystitis (HIC) is an inflammatory subtype of interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome marked by persistent urothelial injury and bladder dysfunction. Bisphenol A (BPA) can disturb redox and inflammatory homeostasis, but its relevance to HIC-associated urothelial vulnerability remains unclear. This study examined whether acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) contributes to BPA-associated ferro-aging-like urothelial injury. Among non-pregnant adult women, higher creatinine-corrected urinary BPA was associated with a phenotype predominantly characterized by urgency urinary incontinence (UUI), and the primary Mendelian randomization analysis suggested higher interstitial cystitis (IC) risk with genetically proxied BPA exposure. Integrated transcriptomic, BPA-target, and machine-learning analyses prioritized ACSL4 as a consistent HIC-associated candidate. HIC tissues showed higher ferro-aging-like transcriptional scores and ACSL4 expression; single-cell analyses further identified disease-associated urothelial cell-state remodeling, with higher ACSL4 expression and SenePy scores in HIC urothelial cells. Structure-based modeling suggested a plausible BPA-ACSL4 interaction, while cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) indicated BPA-associated thermal stabilization of ACSL4. In primary human urothelial cells, BPA increased ACSL4 mRNA and protein expression, lipid peroxidation, iron accumulation, p21 expression, senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-Gal) positivity, inflammatory signaling, and barrier impairment, together with reduced Lamin B1 and ZO-1 expression and transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER). ACSL4 silencing and vitamin C attenuated these changes. In mice, PRGL493 and vitamin C each attenuated multiple BPA-induced bladder abnormalities. Together, these findings support an ACSL4-associated ferro-aging-like urothelial injury phenotype involving iron-lipid stress, senescence-associated changes, inflammation, and barrier impairment, with relevance to selected features of HIC.

papers.title: Developmental sleep during lethargus is associated with metabolic homeostasis and heritable adaptive responses to infection in Caenorhabditis elegans.
papers.authors: Bynedi Seshadhri Chinna Mounish; Kannan Srilekha; Ramesh Anand; Krishnaswamy Balamurugan
papers.abstract: Sleep is a fundamental physiological state essential for metabolic and neuronal homeostasis; however, its contribution to lipid and energy metabolism during development remains incompletely understood. Here, we used Caenorhabditis elegans to investigate the metabolic significance of Developmentally Timed Sleep (DTS). Lethargus-associated DTS was mechanically disrupted using 1 kHz piezoelectric buzzer-induced mechanical stimulation, followed by behavioural, physiological, metabolic and molecular analyses. DTS disruption was associated with reduced behavioural quiescence, altered sleep-associated gene expression, reduced survival and elevated oxidative stress. Notably, disruption during the L4-young adult lethargus window was associated with increased feeding and markedly enhanced lipid accumulation, accompanied by upregulation of the lipid metabolic regulators fat-6, nhr-64 and nhr-80. Despite increased lipid storage, levels of the triglyceride lipase ATGL were elevated, suggesting enhanced lipid mobilization concurrent with persistent lipid accumulation. This metabolic phenotype was accompanied by reduced mitochondrial activity, decreased intracellular ATP, downregulation of atp-3 and activation of AMPK-mediated energy sensing, suggesting energetic stress and potentially inefficient downstream utilization of mobilized lipids. DTS disruption was additionally associated with increased acy-1 and crh-1 expression and enhanced CREB phosphorylation, indicating altered cAMP-CREB-associated neuronal signalling. Furthermore, disruption of DTS in offspring of Salmonella Typhi-infected parents was associated with reduction in their ability to generate heritable adaptive resistance and altered daf-16, sgk-1 and skn-1 mRNA expression. Collectively, these findings suggest that developmental sleep may play a role in lipid storage, mobilization, mitochondrial bioenergetics and cellular energy sensing, with potential consequences for neuronal and adaptive stress responses.

papers.title: Isovitexin Attenuates Aβ-Induced Neurotoxicity by Activating SKN-1/Nrf2 Signaling and Suppressing Ferroptosis in Caenorhabditis elegans Models of Alzheimer’s Disease
papers.authors: Mengjiao Hao; Dongni Wu; Lingli Sun; Xingfei Lai; Ruohong Chen; Zhenbiao Zhang; Qiuhua Li; Suwan Zhang; Xi Zheng; Dongli Li; Shili Sun
papers.venue: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by β-amyloid (Aβ) deposition, oxidative stress, ferroptosis, and mitochondrial dysfunction, while effective therapeutic interventions remain limited. Epidemiological evidence indicates that tea and flavonoids with antiaging properties lower AD risk. In this study, untargeted metabolomic profiling identified isovitexin as a differentially abundant flavonoid in postfermented dark tea (DT), and Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans) AD models were employed to evaluate its anti-AD potential and elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. The results showed that isovitexin significantly extended lifespan, reduced Aβ accumulation, and improved neuromuscular function, demonstrating marked neuroprotective effects. Mechanistically, isovitexin mitigated Aβ-triggered toxicity through SKN-1 signaling, accompanied by the attenuation of Aβ-evoked ferroptosis and mitochondrial dysfunction. Collectively, these results broaden the therapeutic potential of dark tea flavonoids and support further investigation of isovitexin as a candidate for mitigating Aβ-induced neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Lipid-sensing GPR183-KRAS signaling mediates TH17 autoimmunity and identifies fluvoxamine repurposing in uveitis.
papers.authors: Chun Zhang; Xiuxing Liu; Nanwei Xu; Hui Chen; Yuehan Gao; Chenyang Gu; Xinyue Shen; Junying Wu; Xuejing Lu; Pei Zhang; Yuxuan He; Zhuping Xu; Wenru Su
papers.abstract: Autoimmune uveitis (AU) is a leading cause of irreversible blindness driven by pathogenic T helper 17 (TH17) cell-mediated inflammation, yet current therapies are limited by efficacy and side effects, with immunometabolic mechanisms remaining poorly defined. By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing and multilayered metabolomic profiling in patients with AU and experimental AU models, we identified the lipid-sensing G protein-coupled receptor GPR183 as a key immunometabolic regulator in pathogenic CD4+ T cells. Upon activation, GPR183 modulates intracellular signaling via suppression of cyclic adenosine monophosphate-cAMP-dependent protein kinase activity and promotion of son-of-sevenless-dependent KRAS activation, which in turn elicits copper overload-induced mitochondrial oxidative stress, structural impairment, and metabolic rewiring toward glycolysis, thereby promoting TH17 cell pathogenicity. For clinical translation, virtual screening of Food and Drug Administration-approved drugs coupled with molecular docking and microscale thermophoresis validation identified fluvoxamine (FLV) as a direct GPR183 antagonist. In in vivo and in vitro uveitis and colitis models, FLV attenuated GPR183-KRAS signaling, dampened pathogenic TH17 cell responses, and alleviated tissue inflammation. These findings delineate a unique GPR183-KRAS-mitochondrial damage axis governing TH17-driven autoimmunity and support repurposing FLV as a translatable therapeutic approach for AU and other autoimmune inflammatory disorders.

papers.title: A premature ovarian insufficiency-associated LMD-3 point mutation impairs protein stability and causes autophagic-lysosomal dysfunction in Caenorhabditis elegans
papers.authors: Yile Zhai; Tiantian Wang; Meixi Gong; Yuhan Liang; Wenfei Li; Xin Wang; Zhe Zhang
papers.abstract: Reproductive longevity decline characterizes both natural aging and premature ovarian insufficiency (POI). While our previous work established C. elegans LMD-3 as a critical regulator of reproductive capacity, the in vivo consequences of specific clinical mutations remain unclear. Here, we modeled the POI-associated human NCOA7 W804C mutation by engineering the orthologous W690C substitution into the C. elegans lmd-3 locus. We demonstrate that this single-nucleotide substitution severely compromises LMD-3 protein stability and reduces transcript levels. This mutational destabilization is associated with profound systemic autophagic-lysosomal dysfunction, which impairs macromolecular degradation and leads to widespread proteotoxic accumulation of misfolded proteins. Coincident with these organismal defects, mutant animals exhibit an early-onset collapse in reproductive capacity driven by elevated germline apoptosis. Crucially, this pathology is consistent with reduced vitamin B12 availability; mecobalamin supplementation can mitigate the lysosomal block, restoring autophagic flux, proteostasis, and fecundity. These findings elucidate how a clinical mutation drives systemic lysosomal failure and reproductive decline, suggesting vitamin B12 supplementation as a promising metabolic intervention worth further translational exploration.

papers.title: Mitochondria-Targeted Polymer-Lipid Hybrid Nanoprobes for Imaging of K+ and O2 Dynamics in Living Cells.
papers.authors: Tingting Pan; Jiahui Mai; Huili Li; Jianxiang Liao; Yanqing Tian
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial potassium ion (K+) homeostasis and oxygen (O2) level are closely involved in diverse cellular physiological and pathological processes. However, imaging these two parameters within the same subcellular remains challenging because combination of different probes often suffers from spectral crosstalk and mismatched cellular internalization kinetics. Herein, we constructed mitochondria-targeted polymer-lipid hybrid nanoparticles, TPP-KO NPs, for dual-responsive imaging of K+ and O2 dynamics. The nanoprobes were fabricated by a facile self-assembly strategy and were designed with a spatially isolated core-shell architecture to separate the K+- and O2-sensing moieties. In aqueous solution, TPP-KO NPs exhibited concentration-dependent responses to K+ and O2, rapid response kinetics, good colloidal stability, and favorable photostability. Cellular evaluations confirmed their favorable biocompatibility and mitochondrial localization. In living cells, TPP-KO NPs provided distinguishable optical signals of mitochondrial K+ fluctuations and O2 dynamics under the specific excitation and emission ranges after K+-modulating or hypoxic treatments. This dual-responsive nanoprobe system provides an imaging platform for monitoring of mitochondrial K+ and O2 dynamics in living cells, which holds great potential for exploring the mitochondrial K+-O2 microenvironment.

papers.title: Early mitophagy defects and impaired mitochondrial energy metabolism drive target organ damage progression: Lessons from the Fabry heart.
papers.authors: Jessica Gambardella; Antonella Fiordelisi; Federica Andrea Cerasuolo; Antonietta Buonaiuto; Roberta Avvisato; Alessandro Viti; Eduardo Sommella; Pietro Campiglia; Valeria D'Argenio; Nella Prevete; Antonio Pezone; Stefania D'Apice; Giovanna Giuseppina Altobelli; Fahimeh Varzideh; Shivangi Pande; Roberta Paolillo; Cinzia Perrino; Eleonora Riccio; Antonio Pisani; Antonio Bianco; Junichi Sadoshima; Letizia Spinelli; Gaetano Santulli; Daniela Sorriento; Guido Iaccarino
papers.abstract: Increasing evidence supports a pathogenic role for impaired energy metabolism in organ damage. Genetic diseases provide opportunities to investigate these mechanisms, as exemplified by Fabry disease (FD), caused by an α-galactosidase A (GLA) deficiency and globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) accumulation, with cardiomyopathy as the leading cause of death. Beyond Gb3 storage, impaired energy metabolism may contribute to cardiomyopathy. Here, we demonstrate mitochondrial dysfunction in FD heart and its therapeutic targeting. Using a humanized FD mouse model (R301Q-Tg/GLA knockout), embryonic fibroblasts, and neonatal and adult cardiomyocytes, we found impaired mitophagy and mitochondrial respiration, increased reactive oxygen species, and a vicious cycle aggravating lysosomal dysfunction. These defects progressed with age, causing accumulation of dysfunctional mitochondria, energetic failure, apoptosis, cardiac hypertrophy, and diastolic dysfunction. L-arginine, promoting NO/PGC-1α-dependent mitochondrial rescue, prevented cardiac abnormalities. Our findings identify mitochondrial dysfunction as a key driver of FD cardiomyopathy and reveal the lysosome-mitochondria axis as a targetable pathway in FD and beyond.

papers.title: Senescent Mesenchymal Stromal Cells Drive Stem Cell Aging Through Dysregulated Chemokine Synthesis
papers.authors: Shaianne N. Stein; Lorena R. Braid
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Aging is accompanied by a progressive decline in tissue regenerative capacity, driven by intrinsic stem cell dysfunction and age‐associated deterioration of the surrounding stem cell niche. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) are ubiquitous components of stem cell niches, where they integrate structural, metabolic, inflammatory, and paracrine cues to regulate stem cell quiescence, activation, and differentiation. With age, MSCs undergo functional decline and senescence, altering their secretory and signaling profiles. Across tissues, MSC senescence emerges as an intermediate amplifier of aging: molecular, metabolic, epigenetic, and inflammatory stressors promote the senescent state, which converts these upstream insults into chemokine imbalance, chronic inflammation, and progressive loss of stem cell support. Here, we synthesize classical and emerging literature to examine how age‐associated changes in MSC chemokine synthesis contribute to stem cell aging, and we propose a synthesis‐based model in which MSCs translate age‐associated stressors into altered chemokine repertoires that disrupt stem cell‐supportive signaling. We also discuss therapeutic strategies, including chemokine‐directed therapies, senolytics, and MSC rejuvenation, that may restore regenerative capacity by normalizing MSC‐derived signals. Together, the evidence identifies dysregulated chemokine synthesis as a conserved mechanism linking tissue‐resident MSC aging to declining regenerative capacity.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms and therapeutic potential of Rasayana in cellular protection and healthy aging.
papers.authors: Rutuja Gulhane; Neha Nistane; Mohammad Qutub; Amol Tatode; Milind Umekar; Brijesh Taksande; Jayshree Taksande
papers.venue: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
papers.abstract: Aging is a complex biological process characterized by oxidative stress, cellular senescence, and metabolic dysregulation. Ayurveda, the ancient Indian system of medicine, emphasizes longevity and rejuvenation through Rasayana therapy, a specialized branch that enhances vitality, delays aging, and prevents age-related diseases. This review explores the mechanistic basis of Ayurvedic antioxidants, including Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera), Amalaki (Emblica officinalis), Guduchi (Tinospora cordifolia), Shatavari (Asparagus racemosus), Haritaki (Terminalia chebula), Brahmi (Bacopa monnieri), and Curcumin (Curcuma longa), in promoting longevity. These herbs modulate key aging pathways, including oxidative stress reduction, mitochondrial protection, immune modulation, neuroprotection, telomere maintenance, and endocrine balance. Scientific evidence highlights their potential in mitigating chronic inflammation, enhancing cognitive function, and improving metabolic homeostasis, thereby increasing lifespan and healthspan. Systematic electronic database search via PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar with the use of the keywords "Ayurveda," "Rasayana," "antioxidants," "longevity," and "anti-aging herbs" was conducted. English-language peer-reviewed papers were selected on the basis of relevance, mechanistic content, and availability of experimental or clinical evidence. The evidence was collated to identify patterns of therapy and mechanisms in common. Despite promising outcomes, the clinical translation of Ayurvedic antioxidants faces challenges such as limited standardized trials, bioavailability concerns, and regulatory hurdles. Future directions include integrating Ayurvedic principles with modern medicine through personalized therapeutics, nutraceutical innovations, and synergistic formulations. Standardized clinical trials and molecular validation are essential for their acceptance in global healthcare. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of Ayurvedic antioxidants as potent natural interventions for healthy aging.

papers.title: Agnuside from Vitex negundo L. Attenuates Hepatocellular Lipid Accumulation: Association with the AMPK/SREBP1/FASN/HMGCR/PPARα/UCP2 Signaling Network
papers.authors: Abhipsha Saikia; Semim Akhtar Ahmed; Kangkon Saikia; Pranamika Sarma; Devi Basumatary; Ashis K. Mukherjee; Jagat Chandra Borah; Asis Bala
papers.abstract: Abstract Vitex negundo L. (VN) is a medicinal plant known for its anti-inflammatory and hepatoprotective properties, commonly used as a vegetable in northeastern Indian communities. However, its role in treating nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is still underexplored. This study evaluates the therapeutic potential of VN and its bioactive compounds in reducing lipid accumulation in CC1 hepatocytes. A crude extract of VN and its n-butanol fraction (VNBU) were tested on palmitate-induced CC1 hepatocytes to evaluate lipid accumulation. Key compounds Agnuside, 5-hydroxy-3,6,7,3́,4́-pentamethoxyflavone, and Vitexilactone were isolated. Agnuside’s effects on lipogenesis, cholesterol accumulation, and fatty acid oxidation were assessed using biochemical assays and Western blot analysis. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations were conducted to explore its interactions with 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (HMGCR). Agnuside treatment was associated with reduced lipid accumulation by modulating Adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK), HMGCR, Sterol regulatory element-binding transcription factor 1 (SREBP1), Fatty acid synthase (FASN), Peroxisome Proliferator-activated receptors (PPARα), and uncoupling protein (UCP2), suggesting a favorable shift in lipid metabolism. Computational studies indicated that Agnuside binds stably to HMGCR, similar to statins. In summary, these findings suggest that VN and Agnuside exert protective effects in hepatocytes, accompanied by favorable shifts in lipid metabolism markers. Further studies are needed to confirm the causal role of this signaling network.

papers.title: Brain insulin resistance and microglial immunometabolic dysregulation in neurodegenerative diseases
papers.authors: Xinyu Liu; Xiaorong Zhang; Yufang Su; Gaopeng Guan; Xianjun Luo; Puhua Zhang
papers.abstract: Brain insulin resistance (BIR) is increasingly recognized as a contributor to the development and progression of neurodegenerative diseases rather than simply a metabolic abnormality. In the central nervous system, insulin signaling is involved in neuronal survival, synaptic plasticity, energy metabolism, and protein homeostasis. Increasing evidence suggests that impaired brain insulin signaling is associated with Alzheimer disease (AD), Parkinson disease (PD), and other neurodegenerative conditions, although the mechanisms linking BIR to persistent inflammation and neuronal injury remain incompletely understood. Microglia, the principal innate immune cells of the central nervous system, integrate metabolic and immune signals and may therefore provide an important link between impaired insulin signaling and chronic inflammation. BIR may disrupt insulin receptor substrate (IRS), phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K), and protein kinase B (Akt) signaling and promote nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) activation, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, impaired mitophagy, and lysosomal and lipid metabolic disturbances. These changes may promote activation of the NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome, inflammatory mediator release, excessive phagocytosis, and synaptic dysfunction. In turn, persistent microglial inflammation may further impair insulin signaling, forming a reciprocal feedback loop that sustains pathological changes. This review summarizes the mechanisms linking BIR to microglial immunometabolic dysfunction and discusses potential therapeutic strategies targeting metabolic and inflammatory pathways in neurodegenerative diseases.

papers.title: Methylglyoxal Impairs Mitochondrial Bioenergetics and Microglial Functions
papers.authors: Taketo Taguchi; Pamela Maher
papers.abstract: Aging is accompanied by a progressive disruption of brain homeostasis, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying this age-associated deterioration remain poorly understood. Microglia play a critical role in maintaining brain homeostasis by clearing cellular debris and neurotoxic protein aggregates. Here, we investigated the effects of methylglyoxal (MG), a highly reactive endogenous metabolite that accumulates with aging, on microglial functions using the murine microglial cell line BV2. We assessed the effects of MG exposure on multiple aspects of microglial biology in both control and bacterial lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-treated cells, including phagocytic activity, cellular proliferation, cytokine secretion, mitochondrial bioenergetics, mitochondrial membrane potential, and intracellular and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species. We found that MG significantly impaired mitochondrial bioenergetics, leading to reduced cellular energy production, and markedly suppressed multiple essential microglial functions, including phagocytosis. Given the high reactivity of MG with arginine, we also investigated whether arginine depletion contributes to these functional impairments. Arginine depletion recapitulated the impairment of mitochondrial bioenergetics and microglial function induced by MG, demonstrating that arginine availability is a critical determinant of microglial metabolic fitness and immune function. These findings suggest that the age-associated accumulation of MG impairs mitochondrial bioenergetics and microglial functions, thereby potentially accelerating neurodegenerative processes.

papers.title: Screening and evaluation of medicine food homology herbal combinations for ameliorating chemotherapy induced ovarian aging under an integrated multi-strategy framework
papers.authors: Zhang, j.; Chen, X.; Cao, Y.; Liu, Y.; Ning, N.; Bian, W.; Yang, X.; Guo, Y.; Zeng, J.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Ovarian aging poses a serious threat to women's reproductive health. Medicine food homology (MFH) herbs, owing to their favorable safety profile and suitability for long-term use, have become important interventional resources. However, conventional formula screening relies largely on empirical statistics and lacks mechanistic evidence and a systematic screening strategy. Methods: In this study, we integrated single cell transcriptomic analysis, human use evidence mining, UPLC/Q TOF MS chemical profiling and pretrained protein molecular representation models to establish a multi strategy framework for the discovery of MFH herbal combinations. Single cell transcriptomic datasets related to ovarian aging from the GEO database were analyzed to identify key pathological processes and candidate targets. High-frequency MFH herbs were selected by mining classical prescriptions and clinical literature. By comparing six protein molecular pretrained representation combinations, ESM T5 was identified for compound target affinity prediction and validated by molecular dynamics simulation and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assays, ultimately identifying the Astragalus ginseng (Huangqi Renshen) herb pair (HXF) as the core candidate. Functional expression validation of key targets was performed, and the efficacy of HXF and the expression of related molecules were verified in a D gal induced KGN granulosa cell senescence model and a cyclophosphamide-induced rat model of diminished ovarian function. Results: Single cell analysis revealed that ovarian aging was characterized by impaired steroidogenesis, enhanced MDK NCL communication between granulosa cells and immune cells, and extracellular matrix remodeling, with CYP19A1, SERPINE1 and MDK as key targets. By further integrating human-use evidence mining and UPLC/Q TOF MS compound annotation, an MFH compound library comprising 712 molecules was established. ESM T5 prediction, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation and SPR assays confirmed that multiple constituents of Astragalus and ginseng exhibited favorable binding activity toward key targets. At the cellular level, knockdown of MDK or SERPINE1 attenuated the senescence phenotype, whereas knockdown of CYP19A1 aggravated it. In vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrated that Astragalus ginseng ameliorated granulosa cell senescence and diminished ovarian function in rats, restored CYP19A1 related steroidogenesis, downregulated inflammation- and matrix remodeling related molecules such as SERPINE1 and IL18, and reduced MDK NCL colocalization signals. Conclusion: This study established a multi-strategy screening framework integrating disease mechanism decoding, human use evidence constraints and pretrained model prediction, and identified Astragalus ginseng as a candidate herb pair for ameliorating ovarian aging. Its effects may be associated with promoting steroidogenesis, suppressing SERPINE1/IL18 related inflammation and matrix remodeling, and modulating MDK NCL signaling. These findings provide a strategic reference for the mechanism oriented discovery of MFH herbal combinations.

papers.title: In vitro and in silico characterization of human PHOSPHO2 reveals its phospholipid phosphatase activity
papers.authors: Tsunoda, K. A.; Murakami, C.; Sakai, H.; Sakane, F.
papers.abstract: Phosphatidic acid (PA) phosphatase (PAP) is an enzyme that plays a major role in lipid signaling by controlling the cellular levels of two lipid secondary messengers: its substrate, PA, and its product, diacylglycerol. Two types of mammalian PAPs have been reported to date. Type 1 PAP (PAP1) is an Mg2+-dependent, N-ethylmaleimide (NEM)-sensitive cytosolic enzyme (EC 3.1.3.4), whereas type 2 PAP (PAP2), also known as phospholipid phosphatase (PLPP) (EC 3.1.3.113), is an Mg2+--independent, NEM-insensitive transmembrane protein. PAP2 also hydrolyzes other bioactive lipids such as lyso-PA (LPA), sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P), and ceramide-1-phosphate (C1P). Here, we purified human phosphatase orphan 2 (PHOSPHO2), a putative cytosolic phosphatase containing a haloacid dehalogenase-like domain, and characterized its enzymological properties in vitro. Purified PHOSPHO2 displays Mg2+--dependent, NEM-sensitive phosphatase activities toward PA, LPA, S1P, C1P, and glycerol-3-phosphate (G3P) in vitro. Moreover, PHOSPHO2 showed substrate selectivity for PA molecular species containing shorter saturated fatty acids such as lauric acid and myristic acid, or polyunsaturated fatty acids such as docosahexaenoic acid and arachidonic acid. The PAP activity of PHOSPHO2, but not its other phosphatase activities, was strongly enhanced in the presence of phosphatidylcholine and phosphatidylethanolamine, major components of the cell membranes. These results indicate that mammalian PHOSPHO2 is a novel cytosolic PLPP that primarily functions as a PAP on cytoplasm-facing membranes.

papers.title: Mitochondrial Transplantation as a Therapeutic Strategy: From Energy Replacement to Metabolic and Immune Reprogramming.
papers.authors: Chuli Zhu; Meng Xu; Yanan Ji; Jie Wang; Xinlei Yao; Hualin Sun
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction drives diseases, including ischemia-reperfusion injury, neurodegenerative disorders, cardiovascular disease, metabolic syndrome, and inflammation. Conventional mitochondria-targeted strategies offer only partial rescue and are insufficient for severe, irreversible damage. Mitochondrial transplantation (MT)-the delivery of exogenously isolated functional mitochondria to injured cells-has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy that directly restores mitochondrial bioenergetic function and may subsequently modify the tissue microenvironment. This Review examines the entire MT pipeline, from mitochondrial source selection, isolation and preservation, to in vivo delivery strategies. We critically examine the multiple mechanisms underlying MT's therapeutic efficacy, including cellular uptake and intracellular integration, energy restoration and metabolic reprogramming, redox rebalancing, remodeling of mitochondrial quality control (fusion/fission, mitophagy, biogenesis), and immunomodulation. We summarize preclinical and clinical applications across multiple organ systems-heart, nervous system, liver, kidney, lung, skeletal muscle, retina-as well as in oncology and aging. We analyze five major translational bottlenecks: the lack of standardized manufacturing protocols, undefined dose-response relationships, immunogenicity and long-term safety uncertainties, the decisive impact of mitochondrial heterogeneity, and regulatory ambiguity. We outline future directions-mechanistic deepening, engineered target delivery, individualized mitochondrial medicine, combinatorial regimens, and a phased clinical roadmap. MT is not merely energy supplementation; it may reshape cellular metabolism, quality control networks, and immune microenvironments, representing a shift from pharmacological modulation of mitochondrial function toward organelle replacement strategies. Despite challenges, these advances may facilitate individualized mitochondrial therapies as a proposed future direction.

papers.title: The aging secretome as a candidate driver of bone remodeling imbalance: myokines, adipokines, and senescence-associated secretory factors
papers.authors: Hanhong Fang; Xianglong Zhou; Yang Liu; Weicheng Chen; Fulin Zhou; Haoran Zhou; Jianhui Xiang; Liming Xiong
papers.abstract: Bone homeostasis depends on the spatial and temporal coupling of osteoclastic resorption to osteoblastic formation. With aging, this balance shifts toward net bone loss alongside sarcopenia, marrow adipose expansion, and chronic low-grade inflammation. These parallel changes may be linked by a shared set of secreted signals, termed here the aging secretome. We distinguish functional remodeling imbalance, defined as a sustained shift between formation and resorption, from direct uncoupling, in which a resorption-to-formation coupling signal is demonstrably disrupted. The aging secretome comprises three principal arms: muscle-derived signals, including myostatin, irisin, and myogenic extracellular vesicles; fat-derived signals, including leptin, adiponectin, and marrow adipocyte lipotoxicity; and senescence-associated secretory factors, particularly those involving senescent osteocytes, TNF-α, and IL-6. Inflammaging is treated as a shared contextual amplifier rather than a separate signaling arm. These pathways converge on key regulators of skeletal remodeling, including RANKL, Wnt–sclerostin, and IGF-1. This framework also provides a common context for comparing pathway-specific interventions, such as activin type II receptor blockade and sclerostin inhibition, with broader approaches targeting senescence or inflammation. An early phase 2 senolytic trial was negative overall, with only an exploratory signal in women with high senescent-cell burden. The aging secretome should therefore be viewed as an organizing framework whose individual pathways and relative contributions require further validation in human bone.

papers.title: M6A-modified lncRNA RMRP facilitates mitophagy and promotes ox-LDL-induced endothelial cell injury by interacting with PTBP1 and activating the PI3K/AKT pathway.
papers.authors: Ying Fu; Zhu Zhang; Yanqin Yu; Yuanmin Chai; Jinqi Hao; Qinghong Qiao
papers.venue: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Gene regulatory mechanisms
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Endothelial cell dysfunction has been identified as a major risk factor for atherosclerosis. The long non-coding RNA (LncRNA) RNA component of mitochondrial RNA processing endoribonuclease (RMRP) has been detected in mitochondria and is closely associated with inflammation and autophagy. However, the role of the lncRNA RMRP in endothelial cell injury and its potential molecular mechanisms remain unclear. METHODS: Mouse aortic endothelial cells (MAECs) were treated with oxidised low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL). Changes in cell viability, proinflammatory cytokine levels, mitophagy, and mitochondrial membrane potential in MAECs were assessed to investigate the effects of lncRNA RMRP and protein kinase B (AKT3) on endothelial injury. Knockdown and overexpression experiments were performed to determine the effects of lncRNA RMRP, polypyrimidine tract-binding protein 1 (PTBP1), and AKT3 on MAECs stimulated with ox-LDL. RESULTS: Ox-LDL markedly reduced cell viability, increased proinflammatory factor levels, induced mitophagy, and reduced mitochondrial membrane potential in MAECs. Knockdown of lncRNA RMRP attenuated ox-LDL-induced inflammatory responses and mitophagy in MAECs. Knockdown of Methyltransferase-like 14 (METTL14) suppressed the expression of lncRNA RMRP through m6A modification in ox-LDL-treated MAECs. LncRNA RMRP enhanced AKT3 mRNA stability by interacting with PTBP1. LncRNA RMRP promoted ox-LDL-induced mitophagy by targeting AKT3 and stimulating the Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/AKT pathway in MAECs. CONCLUSION: METTL14 regulates the expression of lncRNA RMRP through m6A modification. Overexpressed lncRNA RMRP targets AKT3 by recruiting PTBP1, thus activating the PI3K/AKT pathway to mediate mitophagy and promote the progression of atherosclerosis.

papers.title: SIRT5 deficiency exacerbates sepsis acute renal injury by activating ACSL4/FTH1 axis dependent ferroptosis.
papers.authors: Liliang Jiang; Xi Yu; Guang Shan; Ziqi He; Yongbo Liu; Wenlong Lin; Lingling Song; Zhongyuan Xia
papers.abstract: Sepsis‑associated acute kidney injury (S‑AKI) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in critically ill patients, yet effective targeted therapies remain lacking due to an incomplete understanding of its pathogenesis. Ferroptosis, an iron‑dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, has recently been implicated in AKI, but the upstream regulators of this process in sepsis remain undefined. Here, we identify SIRT5, a mitochondrial NAD ⁺ ‑dependent desuccinylase, as a critical endogenous suppressor of ferroptosis in S‑AKI. Using a cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) murine model and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)‑stimulated HK‑2 proximal tubular cells, we show that SIRT5 expression is significantly downregulated in septic kidney injury. Renal tubular‑specific ablation of Sirt5 exacerbated CLP‑induced renal dysfunction, structural damage, and tubular cell death, whereas AAV9‑mediated SIRT5 overexpression attenuated these pathological changes. Mechanistically, SIRT5 deficiency tipped the balance of the ACSL4/FTH1 axis toward ferroptosis: it increased ACSL4‑dependent membrane lipid remodeling and reduced FTH1‑mediated iron sequestration, accompanied by suppression of the antioxidant enzyme GPX4. Consequently, lipid peroxidation, iron overload, and mitochondrial damage were markedly amplified. Notably, knockdown of ACSL4 in SIRT5‑deficient HK‑2 cells effectively reversed lipid peroxidation, iron accumulation, and cell death, establishing ACSL4 as a key downstream effector of SIRT5‑mediated ferroptosis suppression. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized SIRT5-ACSL4/FTH1 regulatory axis that governs ferroptotic susceptibility in renal tubular cells during sepsis, and suggest that pharmacological restoration of SIRT5 activity or blockade of ACSL4‑driven ferroptosis may offer novel therapeutic avenues for S‑AKI.

papers.title: Xiaoai Jiedu recipe promotes NLRP3 inflammasome activation by alleviating PINK1-mediated mitophagy in hepatocellular carcinoma
papers.authors: Yuan-yuan Wu; Hui-ming Zhu; Zi-yu Lu; Zhuo-hui Tang; Wen-ting Li; Mian-hua Wu
papers.abstract: Background The Xiaoai Jiedu recipe (XJR), a traditional Chinese medicinal formula, has been applied clinically for liver cancer management. XJR exhibits promising anti-tumor potential and may offer a novel strategy for oncological intervention. This study was designed to investigate the molecular mechanisms by which XJR exerts its pharmacological effects against hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods In vivo assays were conducted employing an HCC xenograft mouse model, and HepG2 cells were employed in vitro . ELISA, immunohistochemistry (IHC), immunofluorescence (IF), RT-PCR and western blot were performed to detect PTEN-induced putative kinase 1 (PINK1)-mediated mitophagy and NLRP3 (NOD-like receptor protein 3) inflammasome activation. The cellular mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels were tested with DCFH-DA and MitoSOX. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and JC-1 were utilized to observe the mitochondrial morphology and function, as well as mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) in the process of XJR intervention for HCC. Results XJR prominently promoted pyroptosis by upregulating the related inflammatory cytokines levels in serum and HepG2 cells. The key targets include PINK1, parkin, p62, LC3B, TOMM20, COX IV, NLRP3, ASC, GSDMD, caspase1, IL-1β and IL-18 were observed. XJR disrupted PINK1-mediated mitophagy, which in turn increased mitochondrial ROS levels and promoted NLRP3 inflammasome assembly both in vitro and in vivo . Meanwhile, functional assays using pathway-specific inhibitors and siRNA-mediated knockdown further demonstrated that XJR suppresses mitophagy and enhances NLRP3 inflammasome activation via inhibition of the PINK1/parkin signaling pathway. Conclusions The preliminary results of the present study suggested that XJR may alleviate PINK1-mediated mitophagy and motivate NLRP3 signaling pathway to subsequently exert anti-tumor effects in HCC.

papers.title: AMPK/PINK1/Parkin pathway-associated mitochondrial quality control contributes to magnesium sulfate-induced neuroprotection in postoperative cognitive dysfunction
papers.authors: Guangling Li; Bingqian Fan; Jing Tao; Yu Jiang; Yiwen Hua; Rui Zhan; Xianwen Hu
papers.abstract: Introduction Postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) is associated with neuroinflammation and mitochondrial dysregulation, but the mechanisms linking these processes remain incompletely defined. We investigated the neuroprotective effects of magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄) and the involvement of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)/PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1)/Parkin signaling in experimental POCD. Methods POCD was induced in mice by open tibial fracture under isoflurane anesthesia, and an in vitro inflammatory model was established in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-treated BV2 microglia. Behavioral tests, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, western blotting, TUNEL staining, JC-1 analysis, and adenosine triphosphate (ATP) measurement were used to assess cognition, inflammatory responses, mitochondrial-related metabolic alterations, and pathway-associated changes. Results MgSO₄ improved postoperative behavioral deficits, reduced hippocampal inflammatory cytokines, normalized microglial activation-associated markers, improved cellular ATP levels and mitochondrial membrane potential alterations, and partially normalized mitochondrial dynamics-related protein changes. POCD or LPS reduced PINK1, Parkin, and LC3-II while increasing p62; MgSO₄ partially reversed these changes. MgSO₄ also restored p-AMPK levels, whereas the pharmacological AMPK inhibitor Compound C partially attenuated the effects of MgSO₄ on PINK1/Parkin signaling, ATP levels, inflammatory responses, mitochondrial markers, and behavioral outcomes. Discussion These findings support a model in which AMPK/PINK1/Parkin-related mitochondrial quality control is involved in the neuroprotective effects of MgSO₄ in experimental POCD.

papers.title: Isolation of Ventricular Cardiomyocytes from the Annual Killifish Nothobranchius furzeri for Whole-Cell Patch Clamp Recordings.
papers.authors: Artem V Shamshura; Irina Dzhumaniiazova
papers.abstract: Isolated working cardiomyocytes remain the standard approach for studying cardiac electrophysiology. Single-cell preparations allow for direct investigation and precise measurement of ionic currents and action potentials without the structural complexity of intact cardiac tissue. Nothobranchius furzeri (African turquoise killifish) has rapidly emerged as a prominent model organism for gerontological research due to its exceptionally short lifespan and similarities in aging mechanisms with mammals, including humans. This species combines practical advantages such as small size, inexpensive husbandry, and a rapid life cycle with translational relevance. N. furzeri exhibits age-dependent declines in locomotor activity, cognition, and organ function, accumulation of molecular hallmarks of aging, and sensitivity to pharmacological treatments that modulate lifespan and healthspan. However, investigating the functional decline of the aging heart requires a reliable method to obtain high-quality, viable cells suitable for demanding single-cell techniques. This study optimized a previously described protocol for the isolation of Danio rerio cardiomyocytes to ensure consistent recovery of healthy working myocytes from both young and senescent N. furzeri. This protocol describes the isolation of ventricular cardiomyocytes from N. furzeri specifically optimized for the whole-cell patch clamp technique. The article demonstrates how to efficiently excise the heart, perform enzymatic dissociation of the myocardium by retrograde perfusion, and store the isolated cardiomyocytes. We discuss the selection of enzymes required to digest the extracellular matrix and intercellular junctions without compromising ion channel structure. Freshly isolated cardiomyocytes are suitable for high-resolution electrophysiological assays, including action potential recordings and measurements of major inward and outward ionic currents across age groups. The article also addresses the features of cardiomyocyte isolation in fish that differ from standard mammalian isolation procedures.

papers.title: Long-chain acyl-CoA synthetases in female reproductive diseases: isoform-specific regulation of lipid metabolism, ferroptosis, and inflammatory signaling
papers.authors: Shanyuan Jin; Lin Guo; Zishuo Wu; Zirong Wang; Runyuan Liu; Ying Kong; Hongshuo Zhang
papers.abstract: Female reproductive diseases (FRDs) substantially affect women’s health and fertility, with lipid metabolic reprogramming emerging as a shared pathological feature. Long-chain acyl-CoA synthetases (ACSLs) activate long-chain fatty acids and direct lipid flux toward β-oxidation, lipid synthesis, and phospholipid remodeling, thereby influencing oxidative stress, ferroptosis, and inflammatory signaling. Unlike previous reviews centered on broad ACSL biology, selected isoforms, or pathway-based ferroptosis mechanisms, this review adopts a disease-spanning, isoform-specific framework. We compare ACSL1, ACSL3, ACSL4, ACSL5, and ACSL6 across cervical, ovarian, and endometrial cancers, polycystic ovary syndrome, endometriosis, and preeclampsia. By integrating isoform-specific substrate preference, subcellular localization, and lipid-channeling functions, we examine how individual ACSLs differentially regulate fatty acid oxidation, lipid synthesis and phospholipid remodeling, ferroptosis sensitivity, and inflammatory signaling across reproductive disease contexts. We further distinguish disease-specific experimental evidence from bioinformatic associations and mechanistic extrapolations from other disease models. Current evidence most consistently supports a disease-relevant role for ACSL4 in ferroptosis regulation, whereas ACSL1, ACSL3, ACSL5, and ACSL6 show greater context dependence. This integrated framework identifies shared metabolic mechanisms, disease-specific differences, and priorities for cell-resolved validation and future isoform-selective therapeutic development.

papers.title: Mitochondrial transfer and transplantation in cardiovascular diseases: from signaling pathways to targeted delivery strategies
papers.authors: Yao Xie; Yue Liu; Shasha Xing
papers.abstract: Abstract Mitochondrial dysfunction drives the pathogenesis and progression of various cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). Research has demonstrated that approximately 95% of energy in the heart is supplied by mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), and mitochondria also act as regulators of endothelial cell function, including metabolism, angiogenesis, and survival. Accordingly, mitochondrial-targeted therapies have garnered considerable research interest in CVD treatment. In contrast to traditional drug-based mitochondrial-targeted strategies, mitochondrial transfer and transplantation, as emerging innovative therapeutic approaches, hold great therapeutic promise for alleviating multiple CVDs. This article systematically reviews the molecular mechanisms and regulatory networks of endogenous/intrinsic mitochondrial transfer pathways (tunneling nanotubes, extracellular vesicles, etc.), and comprehensively summarizes the latest preclinical laboratory research, and preliminary early human clinical studies of artificial mitochondrial transplantation in major CVDs, including myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury, myocardial infarction (MI) and heart failure (HF). We further discuss the current critical challenges and potential risks associated with the clinical translation of this strategy, and propose targeted optimization directions and future research perspectives for its clinical application.

papers.title: Piezo1-mitochondrial calcium uniporter coupling-dependent mechanotransduction basis for acupuncture to drive analgesia
papers.authors: Kaifang Yao; Jiaqi Xia; Baomin Dou; Zezhi Fan; Shamim Md. Forhad; Zhihan Chen; Li Ma; Junyi Li; Kaiyuan Deng; Xiaowei Lin; Puyu Niu; Yuxing Fang; Yangyang Liu; Shenjun Wang; Zhifang Xu; Yi Guo
papers.abstract: Abstract Background The mechanosensitive ion channel Piezo1 is a critical sensor of mechanical forces in diverse biological contexts, albeit its role in translating the acupuncture-induced mechanical stimulation into analgesic signaling remains largely unexplored. Acupuncture is a widely used therapy for pain management, with needle manipulation-generated mechanical forces considered central to its therapeutic efficacy. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying this mechanotransduction process remain unknown. Here, we identified myocyte Piezo1 at the ST36 acupoint as a key initiator converting local needling force into peripherally derived analgesic signaling under complete Freund’s adjuvant (CFA)-induced inflammatory pain conditions. Methods In mice with CFA-induced inflammatory pain, we assessed the analgesic efficacy of deep needling at ST36 using paw withdrawal latency tests. The underlying molecular mechanisms were examined through immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, western blotting, transmission electron microscopy, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, electromyography, and in vivo two-photon calcium (Ca) imaging. To evaluate the Piezo1-Ca 2 ⁺-calmodulin (CaM)-Ca 2 ⁺/CaM-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII)-signaling axis and its downstream effects on mitochondrial function and purinergic signaling, we employed muscle-specific adeno-associated virus-mediated knockdown of Piezo1 and CaM together with a panel of pharmacological modulators (GsMTx4, Yoda1, TFP, 2-APB, RU360, DPCPX). Results We first confirmed Piezo1 expression in myocytes within the ST36 acupoint, and muscle-specific Piezo1 knockdown abrogated the analgesic effects of deep needling at ST36. Mechanical stimulation by needling activated Piezo1, thereby triggering Ca 2 ⁺ influx, increasing CaM expression and CaMKII phosphorylation, and enhancing sarcoplasmic reticulum-mitochondrial coupling via the inositol trisphosphate receptor-1 (IP3R1)-glucose-regulated protein 75 (GRP75)-voltage-dependent anion channel-1 (VDAC1) complex and mitochondrial Ca uniporter (MCU) pathway. These events promoted mitochondrial Ca 2 ⁺ uptake and increased adenosine triphosphate (ATP)/adenosine production. Both genetic and pharmacological inhibition of Piezo1, CaM, or downstream signaling molecules blocked the analgesic effects of acupuncture, whereas direct Piezo1 activation with Yoda1 mimicked these effects. In vivo two-photon Ca imaging confirmed that electroacupuncture-evoked myocyte Ca 2 ⁺ transients are Piezo1-dependent, and the resulting adenosine may mediate remote analgesia through the activation of the adenosine A1 receptor. Conclusion Piezo1 acts as a core peripheral mechanotransducer that converts local mechanical stimuli generated by acupuncture into downstream analgesic signaling in CFA-induced inflammatory pain. This study delineates a specific myocyte-originated mechanotransduction axis underlying acupuncture analgesia under inflammatory conditions, thereby providing mechanistic insights for understanding acupoint-specific therapeutic effects.
